title: Sen. Cornyn blocks judicial nominee because Trump didn’t choose Texas | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

GOP Sen. John Cornyn is blocking President Donald Trump’s last-minute nomination of a senior Justice Department official for a federal judgeship as Republicans scramble to confirm Trump’s picks before the end of the year.

The departing Texas senator told CNN on Wednesday he did not return the“blue slip”for the Judiciary Committee to considerT. Elliot Gaiser,exercising the Senate custom to block nominees to judgeships in lawmakers’ home states.

Gaiser currently serves as the head of the Justice Department’s Office of Legal Counsel, and he was nominated earlier this month as an attempt to fill the vacancy before Democrats take over the Senate and the confirmation process hits a standstill.

Cornyn objected to the nomination for the Texas-based seat because it wasn’t going to a Texan.

“I just refuse to be jammed by a non-Texan who has no trial experience, who hasn’t been vetted,” Cornyn said. “And so, we provided the White House an alternative, and I’m hoping they take advantage of it because I don’t want the seat to go vacant either.”

Cornyn has previously suggested former DOJ prosecutor Steve Fahey for the nomination.

As a result of Cornyn’s action, Gaiser didn’t appear at Wednesday’s Judiciary Committee hearing on the last batch of Trump’s nominees.

In a three-hour hearing, seven nominees were asked grueling questions, primarily from Democrats seeking to pin them down on their ability to rule against what the Trump administration would want.

“Just so everybody understands… the reason I’m asking this question is a test of your independence,” Connecticut Democratic Sen. Richard Blumental asked Philip Aubart, nominee for US District Judge for the Middle District of North Carolina.

Some committee members had questions for the nominees about the events of January 6, 2021. Blumenthal expressly asked if anyone on the panel was willing to say that the Capitol was “attacked” on that day, and when no nominees responded, he said, “It’s a sad day.”

Nominees were also frequently questioned on the results of the 2020 presidential election and willingness to rule against the Trump administration.

At the close of Wednesday’s hearing, Sen. Cory Booker condemned the GOP’s haste to fill these judicial seats.

“This is another sad day, another cynical effort, another pathetic attempt, where people are looking at short-term political gain at the cost of the enduring strength of our institutions,” the New Jersey Democrat said.

Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz pushed back, citing the 22 federal judges that were quickly appointed in late 2024, before the Democrats gave up control of Congress and President Joe Biden left office.

Gaiser has issued several OLC opinions in recent months, with many sparking controversies. In early October,CNN reportedthat a classified legal opinion was produced by the Trump administration, justifying lethal strikes against a long list of cartels and suspected drug traffickers. The opinion argued that the strikes were authorized because they posed a threat to Americans.

He went on to tell select members of Congress that the Trump administration can continue these lethal strikes without congressional approval.Gaiser said that those US strikesdid not trigger the requirements of the war powers law because they didn’t meet the definition of “hostilities.”

CNN has reached out to the Justice Department for comment on the Gaiser nomination.

CNN’s Hannah Rabinowitz contributed to this report.
